text.en: The Sangam Tamils earned wealth to do good.

This prose lesson says that Tamils earned wealth and enjoyed doing good, took household life as a life of virtue, and refused acts that would bring blame even if the whole world were the reward. In Sangam times virtue was the centre of human relations, free of religious mixture.
The lesson shows that virtue (அறம்) was seen as a social value that includes charity, truth and justice.
Terms: அறம் (virtue), சங்க இலக்கியம், இல்வாழ்க்கை (household life) and பழி (blame).
